title: Live Diagrams edit ops (v1)
description: Add, connect, change or remove diagram elements in one atomic step (one undo). Describe kinds in plain words ('.NET consumer', 'Kafka topic'); the app picks the icon and position. Put a whole request in one call. The same input as the WebMCP tool edit_diagram and the AI panel's Advanced paste box (which also takes a bare array of ops).

ops.description: Use an empty list only with layout: full to rearrange the existing diagram.

kind.description: Plain words or a stencil id, e.g. 'Kafka topic', 'service.dotnet'.

sublabel.description: Second line, e.g. a topic name 'orders.created'.

key.description: Name to refer to this node later in the same call.

kind.description: async = messages/events; sync = request/response, writes to a database. Left out: sync into a database, gateway, outside or model API, or out of a client or gateway; async into or out of a queue, topic or stream, and otherwise.

relation.description: Leave out for a flow. A dependency instead (dotted, carries no traffic): secret, identity, config, telemetry, deploy or depends, e.g. a service -> Key Vault is secret.

oneOf.description: Put a new node on the connection from -> to: it becomes from -> new -> to. Both new connections keep the old one's kind, relation and props; its label and source side go on the first, its target side on the second.

kind.description: Plain words or a stencil id, e.g. 'Redis cache'.

key.description: Name to refer to the new node later in the same call.

kind.description: Nodes: change the stencil; its connections' relationships follow, as on the canvas (a flow into what becomes a config store turns config; an inferred dependency into what stops being one turns back into a flow), listed in the result's relations. Connections: 'async' or 'sync'.

in.description: Move into this boundary; null removes it from its boundary.

targets.description: Nodes, connections ('A -> B'), boundaries (contents are kept) or notes.

dryRun.description: Validate and report without changing the diagram.

summary.description: One short sentence for the person, e.g. 'Added a Redis cache in front of orders-db'. Shown with the change in the app's AI panel.

$comment: The other tools' inputs are under $tools.

describe_diagram.description: Read the current diagram as compact text: nodes with ids, kinds and labels, connections, boundaries and simulations. Call before editing an existing diagram.

focus.description: Only these elements and their direct neighbours.

Ref.description: An element: id from describe_diagram (preferred), a key set earlier in this call, an exact label, 'label (sublabel)', or for a connection 'From -> To'.

check_diagram.description: Find likely design problems in the current diagram (failed messages that are dropped, topics nobody reads, requests that go round in a circle or chain too deep, a service using another's database, a client going around the gateway, a service that can't keep up or that every request goes through), each naming its elements and, where one exists, a fix as edit_diagram ops. Read-only: apply a fix by sending its ops to edit_diagram. Findings the person ignored aren't listed; only the person can ignore one. With simulations: true it also plays the saved simulations and counts the messages they lose: what happened and where, never a fix (slower: seconds on a large diagram).

rules.description: Only these checks (default: all): dead-letter (failed messages are dropped), no-reader (nobody reads a topic or queue), sync-cycle (requests go round in a circle), sync-chain (requests chained too deep), shared-database (a service uses another's database), entry-gateway (a client goes around the gateway), capacity (a service can't keep up at the diagram's rates), single-point (every request goes through one replica), secret-identity (services read secrets without an identity), schema-registry (Avro or Protobuf on Kafka without a schema registry), dropped (messages a saved simulation loses that no other check explains; only with simulations: true, and never with a fix).

include.description: warnings: likely real problems only; all: suggestions too.

simulations.description: Also play the diagram's saved simulations (each at most 60 s of simulated time, all within about 15 s) and report the messages they lose: counts on findings, and dropped findings. Losses a simulation causes on purpose aren't findings.
